stories.instruction: Let an object derived from a concealed event carry testimony, and choose an audience whose public response makes concealment impossible.

stories.title: Lord Randal (Child Ballad 12)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: Repeated questions gradually expose poisoning and intimate betrayal, allowing bodily symptoms to precede explicit accusation.
stories.analysis: Repeated questions gradually expose poisoning and intimate betrayal, allowing bodily symptoms to precede explicit accusation.
stories.instruction: Reveal a hidden event through a sequence of increasingly specific answers, with each repetition changing the listener's understanding.

stories.title: Sir Patrick Spens (Child Ballad 58)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: An imposed voyage proceeds despite experienced warnings; ominous details make authority's refusal to listen central to the tragedy.
stories.analysis: An imposed voyage proceeds despite experienced warnings; ominous details make authority's refusal to listen central to the tragedy.
stories.instruction: Give an expert a specific warning, a superior a reason to dismiss it, and an irreversible departure after which the warning gains meaning.

stories.title: The Wife of Usher's Well (Child Ballad 79)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: Dead sons return briefly to their mother, but the approaching dawn reasserts separation that desire cannot permanently overturn.
stories.analysis: Dead sons return briefly to their mother, but the approaching dawn reasserts separation that desire cannot permanently overturn.
stories.instruction: Allow a grieving character limited contact with the lost, then make the encounter answer an emotional need without undoing mortality.

stories.title: Little Musgrave and Lady Barnard (Child Ballad 81)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: An affair across unequal social positions triggers violent retaliation, turning private desire into a crisis of status and possession.
stories.analysis: An affair across unequal social positions triggers violent retaliation, turning private desire into a crisis of status and possession.
stories.instruction: Make each member of a triangle pursue a different value, and show how unequal power determines who can enforce consequences.

stories.title: Barbara Allen (Child Ballad 84)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: A refusal becomes irreversible through death; subsequent grief and intertwined grave plants extend attachment beyond reconciliation.
stories.analysis: A refusal becomes irreversible through death; subsequent grief and intertwined grave plants extend attachment beyond reconciliation.
stories.instruction: Give a character a repairable relationship error, delay repair for a specific reason, then decide whether the ending permits or forecloses restitution.

stories.title: The Daemon Lover / House Carpenter (Child Ballad 243)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Traditional ballad; Francis James Child catalogue numbering
stories.teaser: A returning lover offers escape from domestic life but reveals a destructive supernatural destination; variants differ in moral emphasis.
stories.analysis: A returning lover offers escape from domestic life but reveals a destructive supernatural destination; variants differ in moral emphasis.
stories.instruction: Make the invitation answer an unresolved desire, plant contradictory evidence about the destination, and preserve the cost of leaving existing ties.

stories.title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (Samuel Taylor Coleridge)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: An arbitrary killing brings isolation and suffering; partial spiritual recovery does not erase the mariner's recurring need to narrate.
stories.analysis: An arbitrary killing brings isolation and suffering; partial spiritual recovery does not erase the mariner's recurring need to narrate.
stories.instruction: Connect a seemingly small violation to a larger relationship system, and give survival a lasting obligation rather than a clean reset.

stories.title: The Erl-King (Der Erlkönig) (Johann Wolfgang von Goethe)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The child perceives a seductive supernatural pursuer while the father offers ordinary explanations; competing accounts persist through urgent motion.
stories.analysis: The child perceives a seductive supernatural pursuer while the father offers ordinary explanations; competing accounts persist through urgent motion.
stories.instruction: Present the same sensory event through two coherent interpretations, then make urgency prevent complete verification before an irreversible outcome.

stories.title: The Lady of Shalott (Alfred, Lord Tennyson)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A woman sees life through reflections under a prohibition; direct engagement breaks her protected artistic existence.
stories.analysis: A woman sees life through reflections under a prohibition; direct engagement breaks her protected artistic existence.
stories.instruction: Give a creator a rule that protects their work but limits participation, then make an encounter expose what that protection costs.

stories.title: The Eve of St. Agnes (John Keats)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A romantic encounter unfolds within a ritualized expectation of dreams and hostile family surroundings, complicating how desire and perception align.
stories.analysis: A romantic encounter unfolds within a ritualized expectation of dreams and hostile family surroundings, complicating how desire and perception align.
stories.instruction: Make a setting's custom shape expectations, and distinguish what a character experiences from what another character knowingly arranges.

stories.title: Childe Roland to the Dark Tower Came (Robert Browning)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: The speaker advances through a hostile landscape toward an uncertain tower; persistence remains legible even when victory is withheld.
stories.analysis: The speaker advances through a hostile landscape toward an uncertain tower; persistence remains legible even when victory is withheld.
stories.instruction: Give a quest an emotionally binding reason to continue, but let the destination test whether endurance itself is success.

stories.title: The Highwayman (Alfred Noyes)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: Bess's self-sacrificial warning saves her lover from an ambush, but incomplete information later draws him back toward death.
stories.analysis: Bess's self-sacrificial warning saves her lover from an ambush, but incomplete information later draws him back toward death.
stories.instruction: Make one character's protective act succeed locally while delayed knowledge produces a second, tragic decision.

stories.title: Vasilisa the Beautiful
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A mother's doll aids Vasilisa through a hostile household and Baba Yaga's tasks, connecting inherited care to practical survival.
stories.analysis: A mother's doll aids Vasilisa through a hostile household and Baba Yaga's tasks, connecting inherited care to practical survival.
stories.instruction: Give an inherited object limited, relational help, and make the protagonist interpret instructions rather than merely possess a solution.

stories.title: The Death of Koschei the Deathless
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Koschei's death is hidden outside his body within nested containers, turning apparent invulnerability into a problem of locating dependencies.
stories.analysis: Koschei's death is hidden outside his body within nested containers, turning apparent invulnerability into a problem of locating dependencies.
stories.instruction: Map the antagonist's protection as a finite chain of dependencies, and make each layer require a distinct discovery or ally.

stories.title: The Firebird and Tsarevich Ivan
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: The Firebird quest links stolen wonders and dangerous promises; a powerful helper compensates for mistakes without removing their consequences.
stories.analysis: The Firebird quest links stolen wonders and dangerous promises; a powerful helper compensates for mistakes without removing their consequences.
stories.instruction: Let a desired object draw the hero into linked obligations, and give the helper clear limits or expectations that create choices.

stories.title: Sister Alenushka and Brother Ivanushka
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A brother's forbidden drink produces animal transformation while his sister's vulnerability attracts further danger.
stories.analysis: A brother's forbidden drink produces animal transformation while his sister's vulnerability attracts further danger.
stories.instruction: Make a small violation alter a relationship's practical responsibilities, and carry the effect into later scenes rather than treating it as decoration.

stories.title: Father Frost (Morozko)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: Two girls encounter the same winter power under different dispositions; repetition makes treatment and response the basis of comparison.
stories.analysis: Two girls encounter the same winter power under different dispositions; repetition makes treatment and response the basis of comparison.
stories.instruction: Give two characters parallel encounters with a demanding force, then distinguish considerate resilience from a blanket endorsement of abuse.

stories.title: Go I Know Not Whither and Fetch I Know Not What
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A ruler weaponizes an unspecified impossible errand against a subordinate; help turns ambiguity into unexpected capability.
stories.analysis: A ruler weaponizes an unspecified impossible errand against a subordinate; help turns ambiguity into unexpected capability.
stories.instruction: Make the antagonist exploit vague success criteria, and let the protagonist discover a concrete interpretation that changes who controls the task.

stories.title: The Frog Princess (Vasilisa the Wise)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: The frog bride's hidden capabilities challenge appearance-based judgment; destroying her skin too soon breaks the conditions of release.
stories.analysis: The frog bride's hidden capabilities challenge appearance-based judgment; destroying her skin too soon breaks the conditions of release.
stories.instruction: Make a well-intended shortcut violate an ally's stated constraint, then require repair that respects the ally's own knowledge.

stories.title: The Feather of Finist the Falcon
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A secretly visiting falcon lover is separated through hostile interference; the heroine's difficult search turns devotion into sustained action.
stories.analysis: A secretly visiting falcon lover is separated through hostile interference; the heroine's difficult search turns devotion into sustained action.
stories.instruction: Establish a vulnerable meeting arrangement, make interference physically consequential, and let the search demand choices beyond passive longing.

stories.title: The Sea King and Vasilisa the Wise
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: The sea king's daughter solves impossible tasks and enables escape, while later forgetting threatens the bond that made survival possible.
stories.analysis: The sea king's daughter solves impossible tasks and enables escape, while later forgetting threatens the bond that made survival possible.
stories.instruction: Give the helper independent stakes, then test whether the protagonist remembers and honors that assistance after entering safety.

stories.title: Twelve Months
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.attribution: Slavic/Eastern European folk tradition; version unspecified
stories.teaser: A girl sent for out-of-season goods receives aid from personified months; greedy imitation fails to reproduce the original relationship.
stories.analysis: A girl sent for out-of-season goods receives aid from personified months; greedy imitation fails to reproduce the original relationship.
stories.instruction: Turn an impossible demand into an encounter with the system governing it, and distinguish respectful requests from entitlement.

stories.title: The Tale of Tsar Saltan (Alexander Pushkin)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: False messages separate a ruler from his wife and son; marvels and disguised visits rebuild the possibility of recognition.
stories.analysis: False messages separate a ruler from his wife and son; marvels and disguised visits rebuild the possibility of recognition.
stories.instruction: Give a family rupture a specific communication failure, identify who controls the channel, and make reunion depend on independently verifiable evidence.

stories.title: The Tale of the Golden Cockerel (Alexander Pushkin)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A king accepts an extraordinary warning device but resists its provider's claim, bringing political power into conflict with an earlier promise.
stories.analysis: A king accepts an extraordinary warning device but resists its provider's claim, bringing political power into conflict with an earlier promise.
stories.instruction: Make a ruler's advantage depend on a debt they expect power to cancel, then design a consequence power cannot simply command away.

stories.title: The Tale of the Dead Princess and the Seven Knights (Alexander Pushkin)
stories.section: European Fairytales, Folk Traditions & Narrative Ballads
stories.teaser: A jealous queen pursues a displaced princess despite refuge among seven knights; repeated inquiry keeps the distant threat active.
stories.analysis: A jealous queen pursues a displaced princess despite refuge among seven knights; repeated inquiry keeps the distant threat active.
stories.instruction: Let an antagonist receive periodic evidence that the target survives, and use each confirmation to motivate a new tactic rather than random recurrence.

stories.title: The Iliad (Homer)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Achilles' quarrel with Agamemnon removes a crucial fighter; Patroclus' death redirects wounded honor into devastating grief and revenge.
stories.analysis: Achilles' quarrel with Agamemnon removes a crucial fighter; Patroclus' death redirects wounded honor into devastating grief and revenge.
stories.instruction: Connect a protagonist's personal grievance to a collective dependency, then make the cost fall on someone whose loss changes the grievance's meaning.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The quarrel and Achilles' withdrawal
children.analysis: Agamemnon's seizure of Briseis makes Achilles withdraw, exposing the army's dependence on a person its leader humiliates.
children.instruction: Give an institution a crucial contributor whose dignity it violates, then make withdrawal reveal a dependency leaders assumed they could ignore.

children.title: The embassy to Achilles
children.analysis: Offers and personal appeals fail to restore Achilles' participation, exposing differences between compensation, trust, and honor.
children.instruction: Let several negotiators offer distinct reasons for return, and specify which unmet need makes material compensation insufficient.

children.title: Patroclus borrows Achilles' armor
children.analysis: Patroclus enters battle wearing another man's armor, making reputation effective while exposing the wearer to risks beyond its protection.
children.instruction: Separate a borrowed identity's deterrent effect from the borrower's actual capacity, and make crossing a stated limit consequential.

children.title: Achilles returns against Hector
children.analysis: Patroclus' death changes Achilles' priority from vindication to retaliation, with victory failing to restore the lost relationship.
children.instruction: Make a loss replace the original goal, and show what achieving the replacement cannot recover.

children.title: Priam seeks Hector's body
children.analysis: Priam's appeal makes enemies encounter one another through parental grief and mortality, interrupting retaliatory distance.
children.instruction: Give an enemy a request grounded in a vulnerability the protagonist also knows, and let recognition change one concrete action without erasing the conflict.

stories.title: The Odyssey (Homer)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Odysseus' return requires surviving strange hosts and concealing identity at home; recognition must distinguish loyalty from opportunism.
stories.analysis: Odysseus' return requires surviving strange hosts and concealing identity at home; recognition must distinguish loyalty from opportunism.
stories.instruction: Make returning home a second challenge after physical arrival, and reveal identity selectively through tests tied to shared history.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The Cyclops
children.analysis: Odysseus' false name enables escape, but announcing his identity afterward lets the injured Cyclops direct a consequential appeal against him.
children.instruction: Let a successful deception require continued anonymity, then tempt the protagonist to sacrifice safety for recognition.

children.title: Circe and the transformed crew
children.analysis: Companions' transformation makes approaching Circe a rescue problem; resistance and negotiation alter a hostile encounter into assistance.
children.instruction: Give a powerful opponent one bounded method of control, then establish what allows negotiation without simply matching their power.

children.title: The visit to the dead
children.analysis: Seeking guidance among the dead brings practical warnings alongside encounters that expose the limits of heroic reputation and survival.
children.instruction: Pair an information-seeking mission with a personal encounter that changes how the requested information will be used.

children.title: The Sirens
children.analysis: Odysseus arranges restraint before hearing a temptation he expects to overpower his judgment.
children.instruction: Let a character anticipate their own weakness and delegate enforcement of a chosen limit before the moment of temptation.

children.title: Scylla and Charybdis
children.analysis: Passage between dangers makes avoidance of all harm impossible, placing a leader inside a decision with unequal losses.
children.instruction: Define incompatible safety objectives, make the available information clear, and show who bears the cost of the chosen route.

children.title: The cattle of Helios
children.analysis: Hunger and delayed travel undermine a prohibition, showing how a group's immediate needs strain a leader's instruction.
children.instruction: Make a rule's long-term protection compete with acute deprivation, and distinguish the leader's decision from the group's independent action.

children.title: The bow contest and the suitors
children.analysis: A contest centered on Odysseus' bow allows concealed identity and distinctive competence to converge at home.
children.instruction: Choose an established skill that can verify identity publicly, and explain why the test occurs before the claim is announced.

children.title: Penelope's bed test
children.analysis: Penelope tests the returned man's knowledge of their immovable bed, using shared material history rather than appearance alone.
children.instruction: Give an intimate recognition scene a detail known through lived experience, and let the skeptical character control the verification.

stories.title: Virgil's Aeneid
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Aeneas' promised future demands departures and warfare; public destiny repeatedly conflicts with intimate attachment and mercy.
stories.analysis: Aeneas' promised future demands departures and warfare; public destiny repeatedly conflicts with intimate attachment and mercy.
stories.instruction: Give a long-term mission credible collective value, then dramatize specific people who bear its cost rather than treating destiny as automatic justification.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The fall of Troy and departure
children.analysis: Aeneas' account of Troy's destruction gives departure meaning through the people and sacred objects he carries forward.
children.instruction: At a catastrophe, force the protagonist to choose what can be saved, making those choices define the future community.

children.title: Dido and the departure from Carthage
children.analysis: Aeneas' departure toward Italy makes his public mission incompatible with Dido's attachment and political situation.
children.instruction: Make both possible futures concrete, and show the abandoned person's costs rather than using them only to prove the hero's resolve.

children.title: The underworld and future Rome
children.analysis: The visit to the dead joins personal losses to a vision of future descendants, enlarging the mission while framing it ideologically.
children.instruction: Let a vision connect private memory to collective purpose, and preserve the possibility that its framing omits the mission's costs.

children.title: The war with Turnus
children.analysis: Aeneas' last confrontation turns on a reminder of Pallas, making personal revenge shape the act that closes the war.
children.instruction: After an opponent is defeated, give the protagonist a final discretionary choice triggered by a planted object or memory.

stories.title: The Argonautica (Apollonius of Rhodes)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Jason's expedition depends on diverse helpers and Medea's decisive assistance, making the prize inseparable from obligations created during acquisition.
stories.analysis: Jason's expedition depends on diverse helpers and Medea's decisive assistance, making the prize inseparable from obligations created during acquisition.
stories.instruction: List which indispensable help makes a quest possible, and carry the resulting debts into the supposedly successful return.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The Argonauts gather
children.analysis: The expedition gathers heroes whose abilities exceed any single leader's competence, making coordination part of the quest.
children.instruction: Make recruitment answer specific anticipated problems, and give the leader a function other than being best at every task.

children.title: The Clashing Rocks
children.analysis: Passage through the rocks requires guidance and timing rather than straightforward force.
children.instruction: Give a threshold a repeatable physical rule and a narrow timing window, then make the crossing depend on trust in another observer.

children.title: Medea and the tasks of Aeetes
children.analysis: Jason's success depends on Medea's knowledge and assistance against tasks controlled by her father.
children.instruction: Give the local helper information outsiders lack and a personal reason to risk using it, then preserve the debt after success.

children.title: The escape from Colchis
children.analysis: Departure with the fleece brings pursuit and violent costs, making the acquired prize inseparable from methods used to keep it.
children.instruction: Make escape force choices about limits, and carry complicity into the return rather than treating possession of the prize as moral closure.

stories.title: The Thebaid (Statius)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The brothers' struggle over Thebes draws allies into inherited hostility; reciprocal claims turn succession into collective catastrophe.
stories.analysis: The brothers' struggle over Thebes draws allies into inherited hostility; reciprocal claims turn succession into collective catastrophe.
stories.instruction: Make rival claimants' goals mutually exclusive, then show how each appeal to allies widens the human cost of a private dispute.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The brothers' contested succession
children.analysis: Thebes' succession dispute sets brothers against one another and draws external allies into their incompatible claims.
children.instruction: Give each claimant a plausible rule of legitimacy and show why accepting one requires the other to surrender something central.

children.title: Hypsipyle and Opheltes
children.analysis: The expedition's delay intersects with a child's death and commemorative games, interrupting martial momentum with a different kind of responsibility.
children.instruction: Use a side episode to expose the human obligations a main quest overlooks, making its consequences alter the group's priorities.

children.title: The brothers' duel and its aftermath
children.analysis: The brothers' confrontation destroys both, leaving burial and surviving relationships to carry the unresolved conflict.
children.instruction: Let symmetrical revenge exhaust its original participants, then give survivors a choice about whether to perpetuate its rules.

stories.title: The Achilleid (Statius)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The unfinished Achilleid follows Achilles' hidden upbringing on Scyros and exposure through martial inclinations; it does not complete his life story.
stories.analysis: The unfinished Achilleid follows Achilles' hidden upbringing on Scyros and exposure through martial inclinations; it does not complete his life story.
stories.instruction: Make a protective disguise conflict with a desire or trained response, and let discovery arise from that pressure rather than coincidence.
notes: Unfinished epic. No completed Achilles biography is implied.
Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Achilles concealed on Scyros
children.analysis: Thetis hides Achilles among girls to delay his martial fate, placing parental protection against the emerging warrior's identity.
children.instruction: Make protective concealment workable but costly to the concealed person's desires, and give both perspectives intelligible stakes.

children.title: Ulysses exposes Achilles
children.analysis: A staged display of weapons and alarm draws Achilles toward a martial response, making practiced inclination reveal concealed identity.
children.instruction: Give a disguised character a deeply trained response, then construct a test that activates it without requiring impossible mind-reading.

stories.title: The Works and Days (Hesiod)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Hesiod combines address to Perses, myths, and practical counsel to connect household conduct with justice and survival.
stories.analysis: Hesiod combines address to Perses, myths, and practical counsel to connect household conduct with justice and survival.
stories.instruction: Use brief examples to test a character's competing principles, and embed advice in a concrete livelihood conflict rather than abstract exposition.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Prometheus, Pandora, and the burden of work
children.analysis: The linked myths explain labor and human vulnerability through conflicts and gifts whose effects exceed immediate intentions.
children.instruction: Use an origin episode to establish a present constraint, then show how characters contest its moral explanation.

children.title: The five races
children.analysis: Hesiod's succession of races distinguishes kinds of human life and judgment, including a heroic race that complicates simple linear decline.
children.instruction: Make historical stages differ in conduct and institutions, preserving exceptions that challenge an overly neat progress or decline narrative.

children.title: The hawk and the nightingale
children.analysis: A predator's speech states the logic of superior force within a broader argument about justice.
children.instruction: Let an embedded fable articulate a powerful character's worldview, then test it against the surrounding story rather than presenting it as neutral truth.

stories.title: The Theogony (Hesiod)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Divine generations establish order through birth, suppression, and overthrow; attempts to prevent succession help perpetuate conflict.
stories.analysis: Divine generations establish order through birth, suppression, and overthrow; attempts to prevent succession help perpetuate conflict.
stories.instruction: Give rulers a specific fear of replacement, then make their preventive policy produce the coalition capable of replacing them.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Cronus overthrows Uranus
children.analysis: Uranus' suppression of his children creates the coalition and opportunity for his overthrow.
children.instruction: Make a ruler's attempt to prevent replacement impose costs that give potential rivals a shared cause.

children.title: Zeus survives Cronus
children.analysis: Rhea's substitution allows one child to survive a ruler's repeated attempt to consume possible successors.
children.instruction: Give a repetitive control mechanism one plausible verification weakness, and let a caregiver exploit it with limited resources.

children.title: The Titanomachy
children.analysis: Zeus' conflict with the Titans depends on alliances and the power of beings earlier confined.
children.instruction: Make releasing an excluded group change the balance of conflict, and specify what settlement or recognition their help creates.

children.title: Zeus and Typhoeus
children.analysis: Typhoeus threatens the new divine order after earlier succession struggles, testing whether the settlement can endure a different kind of opponent.
children.instruction: After a victory, introduce a threat to the system's operation rather than another identical claimant to its throne.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Demeter
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Demeter's loss becomes a crisis for gods and humans when withheld fertility makes private grief materially unavoidable.
stories.analysis: Demeter's loss becomes a crisis for gods and humans when withheld fertility makes private grief materially unavoidable.
stories.instruction: Give an overlooked figure control of an essential system, and make negotiation depend on recognizing a harm others initially dismiss.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Apollo
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Apollo's birth and establishment of sacred authority link divine identity to places, witnesses, and the creation of worship.
stories.analysis: Apollo's birth and establishment of sacred authority link divine identity to places, witnesses, and the creation of worship.
stories.instruction: Make founding legitimacy depend on public acts and local resistance, distinguishing a claimed title from the institutions that sustain it.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Hermes
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Hermes' theft and musical invention lead from conflict with Apollo to negotiated recognition within divine order.
stories.analysis: Hermes' theft and musical invention lead from conflict with Apollo to negotiated recognition within divine order.
stories.instruction: Let a disruptive newcomer create both a problem and a valuable innovation, making settlement require exchange rather than simple punishment.

stories.title: Homeric Hymn to Aphrodite
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.attribution: Anonymous Homeric Hymn tradition; not assumed authored by Homer
stories.teaser: Aphrodite experiences desire for a mortal, revealing vulnerability within the power she normally exercises over others.
stories.analysis: Aphrodite experiences desire for a mortal, revealing vulnerability within the power she normally exercises over others.
stories.instruction: Put an influential character under their own system's pressures, then make the resulting relationship expose costs they previously externalized.

stories.title: Prometheus Bound (Aeschylus)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Prometheus' physical confinement shifts conflict into endurance, testimony, and contested knowledge of the future; attribution to Aeschylus is debated.
stories.analysis: Prometheus' physical confinement shifts conflict into endurance, testimony, and contested knowledge of the future; attribution to Aeschylus is debated.
stories.instruction: When action is physically constrained, give the protagonist consequential information and choices about disclosure, allegiance, or refusal.
notes: Attribution to Aeschylus is disputed.

stories.title: Agamemnon (Aeschylus)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Agamemnon's homecoming brings war's triumph into a household structured by prior sacrifice and revenge.
stories.analysis: Agamemnon's homecoming brings war's triumph into a household structured by prior sacrifice and revenge.
stories.instruction: Let public success conceal an unresolved domestic debt, and make the ceremonial welcome carry evidence of that debt.

stories.title: Oedipus Rex (Sophocles)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Oedipus' attempt to save Thebes through investigation uncovers his own identity and involvement in the city's crisis.
stories.analysis: Oedipus' attempt to save Thebes through investigation uncovers his own identity and involvement in the city's crisis.
stories.instruction: Make each valid clue advance the external investigation while destabilizing the investigator's self-understanding; avoid solving the mystery through withheld arbitrary facts.

stories.title: Oedipus at Colonus (Sophocles)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The aged Oedipus becomes politically valuable despite earlier exclusion, transforming a displaced person's destination into a contested source of power.
stories.analysis: The aged Oedipus becomes politically valuable despite earlier exclusion, transforming a displaced person's destination into a contested source of power.
stories.instruction: Let a rejected character possess a newly relevant resource, and make renewed offers reveal whether others respect the person or merely want that resource.

stories.title: Antigone (Sophocles)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Antigone's burial duty conflicts with Creon's decree; each side's absolutism narrows opportunities for correction.
stories.analysis: Antigone's burial duty conflicts with Creon's decree; each side's absolutism narrows opportunities for correction.
stories.instruction: Give opposing characters intelligible obligations, identify a possible compromise, and show the choices that make it unavailable.

stories.title: Medea (Euripides)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Medea's revenge against Jason destroys attachments she also values, making retaliation inseparable from catastrophic self-inflicted loss.
stories.analysis: Medea's revenge against Jason destroys attachments she also values, making retaliation inseparable from catastrophic self-inflicted loss.
stories.instruction: Give revenge a cost the avenger understands and values, and show the decision that ranks injury to the enemy above preserving that value.

stories.title: The Bacchae (Euripides)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Pentheus' attempt to police Dionysian worship draws him into the spectacle he seeks to control, ending in fatal misrecognition.
stories.analysis: Pentheus' attempt to police Dionysian worship draws him into the spectacle he seeks to control, ending in fatal misrecognition.
stories.instruction: Make an authority's curiosity or repression expose them to the system they deny, and turn their surveillance method into vulnerability.

stories.title: Hippolytus (Euripides)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Concealed desire, a damaging accusation, and a father's punitive response destroy Hippolytus before the account can be corrected.
stories.analysis: Concealed desire, a damaging accusation, and a father's punitive response destroy Hippolytus before the account can be corrected.
stories.instruction: Give a false accusation persuasive context and an authority a reason to act quickly, then track which verification opportunity is refused.

stories.title: Creation and the Four Ages of Man
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Ovid moves from creation to successive ages, compressing moral and material change into a patterned account of decline.
stories.analysis: Ovid moves from creation to successive ages, compressing moral and material change into a patterned account of decline.
stories.instruction: Design historical stages around concrete changes in institutions or everyday behavior, and clarify whose perspective labels a stage better or worse.

stories.title: Deucalion and Pyrrha (The Flood)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Flood survivors interpret a sacred instruction through an unexpected meaning, turning remnants of earth into a renewed human population.
stories.analysis: Flood survivors interpret a sacred instruction through an unexpected meaning, turning remnants of earth into a renewed human population.
stories.instruction: Let rebuilding depend on reinterpreting an ambiguous instruction, and make the solution arise from the setting's symbolic logic.

stories.title: Apollo and Daphne
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: Daphne's escape from pursuit takes the form of bodily transformation, while Apollo claims an emblem from the changed body.
stories.analysis: Daphne's escape from pursuit takes the form of bodily transformation, while Apollo claims an emblem from the changed body.
stories.instruction: Make an escape solve immediate danger while imposing a lasting cost, and distinguish the pursuer's interpretation from the target's autonomy.

stories.title: Phaethon and the Sun Chariot
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics

children.instruction: Use a relationship goal to connect varied trials, but let each trial change the seeker's understanding rather than only postpone reunion.

stories.title: The Conference of the Birds (Mantiq al-Tayr) (Farid ud-Din Attar)
stories.section: Classical Mythologies, Sagas & Epics
stories.teaser: The birds' search for the Simurgh culminates in recognition that transforms the distinction between seekers and sought.
stories.analysis: The birds' search for the Simurgh culminates in recognition that transforms the distinction between seekers and sought.
stories.instruction: Let a quest's obstacles expose the seekers' different attachments, and make the ending reinterpret a goal established from the beginning.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The valley of the quest
children.analysis: The first named valley makes entering the search a demand on the seeker's prior attachments within Attar's spiritual allegory.
children.instruction: Give a quest's entrance a concrete relinquishment, making commitment visible before the first external victory.

children.title: The valley of love
children.analysis: Love's valley challenges calculating self-interest within the poem's mystical progression.
children.instruction: Let a character's commitment make an earlier decision rule inadequate, while preserving consequences rather than glorifying recklessness automatically.

children.title: The valley of knowledge
children.analysis: The knowledge stage treats understanding as dependent on the seeker's path and capacity.
children.instruction: Give companions different partial insights and require them to revise assumptions without making all interpretations equally supported.

children.title: The valley of detachment
children.analysis: Detachment changes the significance of gains that once organized desire.
children.instruction: Revisit an earlier prize after growth and make the protagonist's changed response visible through a practical choice.

children.title: The valley of unity
children.analysis: The allegory questions distinctions that previously separated the seeker from the sought.
children.instruction: Plant recurring parallels between a goal and the people pursuing it, allowing a later revelation to reinterpret them.

children.title: The valley of bewilderment
children.analysis: Bewilderment disrupts confident categories rather than supplying another simple answer.
children.instruction: Let a revelation undermine the protagonist's explanatory model, and give them a meaningful next action despite incomplete certainty.

children.title: The valley of poverty and annihilation
children.analysis: The final valley brings the seeker's self-understanding into the poem's culmination; translations vary in naming.
children.instruction: Make the ending resolve a planted identity question rather than merely deliver an object, and label the adaptation's secular or spiritual interpretation.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Bala Kanda (The Boyhood of Rama)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Rama's early training and marriage test connect education, extraordinary capacity, and public recognition before the larger crisis.
stories.analysis: Rama's early training and marriage test connect education, extraordinary capacity, and public recognition before the larger crisis.
stories.instruction: Establish the protagonist's values through a limited early trial, then reuse its competencies under more difficult moral conditions later.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Ayodhya Kanda (The Exile of Rama)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: A prior royal promise redirects succession into Rama's exile, testing obligations among ruler, spouses, brothers, and subjects.
stories.analysis: A prior royal promise redirects succession into Rama's exile, testing obligations among ruler, spouses, brothers, and subjects.
stories.instruction: Make an old commitment newly enforceable at a public transition, and show how each family member interprets duty differently.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Aranya Kanda (The Forest Life & Abduction of Sita)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Forest exile becomes a separation crisis through an enticing diversion and Ravana's abduction of Sita; details vary by telling.
stories.analysis: Forest exile becomes a separation crisis through an enticing diversion and Ravana's abduction of Sita; details vary by telling.
stories.instruction: Give an adversary a coordinated plan that separates protectors, and maintain the abducted character's perspective and agency in subsequent scenes.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Kishkindha Kanda (Alliance with Sugriva and Hanuman)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Rama's search becomes linked to Sugriva's struggle with Vali, making assistance depend on another community's contested leadership.
stories.analysis: Rama's search becomes linked to Sugriva's struggle with Vali, making assistance depend on another community's contested leadership.
stories.instruction: Build an alliance from two specific unmet goals, then examine whether the means of satisfying one compromise the other's stated principles.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Sundara Kanda (Hanuman's Leap to Lanka)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: Hanuman's crossing, search, meeting with Sita, and return make information and reassurance central achievements before military victory.
stories.analysis: Hanuman's crossing, search, meeting with Sita, and return make information and reassurance central achievements before military victory.
stories.instruction: Give an infiltration mission separate objectives for locating, communicating, verifying, and returning, so success is more than reaching the target.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Yuddha Kanda (The Great Battle of Lanka)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: The Lanka campaign coordinates allies and extraordinary weapons while making rescue, kingship, and the treatment of Sita contested concerns.
stories.analysis: The Lanka campaign coordinates allies and extraordinary weapons while making rescue, kingship, and the treatment of Sita contested concerns.
stories.instruction: Track military success and relational repair as separate objectives, and show who must act after the enemy is defeated.

stories.title: Valmiki Ramayana: Uttara Kanda (The Final Trial and Ascension)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ramayana traditionally attributed to Valmiki; textual variation
stories.teaser: The Uttara Kanda revisits kingship, public suspicion, Sita's exclusion, and the next generation; its textual status and interpretation vary.
stories.analysis: The Uttara Kanda revisits kingship, public suspicion, Sita's exclusion, and the next generation; its textual status and interpretation vary.
stories.instruction: Use an aftermath to test whether the restored order protects those who paid for it, preserving excluded characters' claims rather than assuming public approval is justice.
notes: The Uttara Kanda's textual history and interpretation are contested; source tradition and adaptation should be identified.

stories.title: Dutt's Condensed Ramayana & Mahabharata Epics
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Dutt's paired adaptations condense two epics, making selection and emphasis part of the storytelling rather than a replacement for every source episode.
stories.analysis: Dutt's paired adaptations condense two epics, making selection and emphasis part of the storytelling rather than a replacement for every source episode.
stories.instruction: When adapting a vast source, choose a clear causal and emotional spine and record which episodes are omitted, merged, or reframed.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Dutt's condensed Ramayana
children.analysis: Dutt's selection presents a shortened route through Rama's story, emphasizing chosen dramatic episodes rather than every source passage.
children.instruction: For a condensed adaptation, preserve the decisions that connect exile, alliance, rescue, and aftermath, identifying omissions explicitly.

children.title: Dutt's condensed Mahabharata
children.analysis: The companion adaptation selects major moments of dynastic conflict and consequence from a much larger work.
children.instruction: Condense by causal turning points, retaining the aftermath needed to judge the victory rather than ending automatically at the battle.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Adi Parva (The Book of Beginnings & Shakuntala)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The Adi Parva establishes lineages, births, rivalries, and embedded stories that give later succession conflicts their stakes.
stories.analysis: The Adi Parva establishes lineages, births, rivalries, and embedded stories that give later succession conflicts their stakes.
stories.instruction: Introduce only ancestry that changes a present claim or relationship, and attach each lineage fact to a future decision it constrains.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Shakuntala and recognition
children.analysis: The epic's Shakuntala episode concerns recognition of a woman, a prior union, and her son's claim; later dramatic versions add different devices.
children.instruction: Ground a recognition dispute in explicit prior commitments, and do not import the ring-and-curse mechanism without naming a different adaptation.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Sabha Parva (The Book of the Assembly Hall & Dice Game)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The dice game turns accepted court procedure into dispossession and public violation, exposing failures of authority within an apparently lawful setting.
stories.analysis: The dice game turns accepted court procedure into dispossession and public violation, exposing failures of authority within an apparently lawful setting.
stories.instruction: Give an antagonist a respected procedure to exploit, and identify the witnesses whose refusal to intervene makes the harm possible.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Vana Parva (Forest Exile, Nala and Damayanti, Savitri and Satyavan)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The forest book places the exiled Pandavas beside narratives such as Nala and Savitri, using other lives to examine their predicament.
stories.analysis: The forest book places the exiled Pandavas beside narratives such as Nala and Savitri, using other lives to examine their predicament.
stories.instruction: Insert a secondary story only when its dilemma changes how a main character understands or acts on the present crisis.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Nala and Damayanti
children.analysis: Gambling and displacement break a royal household, while disguise and recognition shape the possibility of reunion.
children.instruction: Make a relationship survive changed status through specific remembered conduct, and give both partners active strategies during separation.

children.title: Savitri and Satyavan
children.analysis: Savitri follows Death and uses successive exchanges and boons to secure a future that depends on her husband's life.
children.instruction: Give a negotiator limits they must respect, then let carefully connected requests expose a route through those limits.

children.title: The questions at the lake
children.analysis: A deadly encounter at a lake makes answering questions and choosing fairly more important than immediate strength.
children.instruction: Place an urgent bodily need behind a warning, and let the successful character pause to understand the condition others ignored.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Virata Parva (Incognito Year at Virata's Court)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The Pandavas' concealed year requires capable people to limit public displays until a time-bound condition is satisfied.
stories.analysis: The Pandavas' concealed year requires capable people to limit public displays until a time-bound condition is satisfied.
stories.instruction: Define what would expose each hidden identity, then make a legitimate duty compete with remaining undetected until the deadline.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Udyoga Parva (War Council & Peace Negotiations)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Diplomatic efforts and competing demands establish what might avert war and why the available settlement fails.
stories.analysis: Diplomatic efforts and competing demands establish what might avert war and why the available settlement fails.
stories.instruction: Specify each side's minimum acceptable terms and a credible compromise, then show the decision that closes the peaceful route.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Bhishma Parva (Bhishma's Command & The Bhagavad Gita)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Arjuna's battlefield hesitation opens the Gita's inquiry into action and obligation within an imminent war, not an abstract motivational pause.
stories.analysis: Arjuna's battlefield hesitation opens the Gita's inquiry into action and obligation within an imminent war, not an abstract motivational pause.
stories.instruction: Give a protagonist two deeply held duties that conflict in one immediate act, and let guidance clarify the conflict without erasing its human stakes.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Drona Parva (Fall of Abhimanyu & Death of Drona)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Abhimanyu's death and the effort to defeat Drona expose how tactical advantage tests commitments to fair conduct.
stories.analysis: Abhimanyu's death and the effort to defeat Drona expose how tactical advantage tests commitments to fair conduct.
stories.instruction: Establish battle rules and information limits before breaking them, then carry the resulting moral and relational debts beyond the victory.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Karna Parva (Karna's Leadership & Duel with Arjuna)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Karna's final combat carries accumulated loyalties, revelations, curses, and disadvantages into a duel whose meaning exceeds skill alone.
stories.analysis: Karna's final combat carries accumulated loyalties, revelations, curses, and disadvantages into a duel whose meaning exceeds skill alone.
stories.instruction: Plant a formidable opponent's constraints across earlier scenes, and distinguish structural disadvantage from personal failure in the final encounter.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Shalya Parva (Duryodhana's Last Stand)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Duryodhana's last stand and the decisive mace duel leave the winners' methods open to dispute even as military resistance collapses.
stories.analysis: Duryodhana's last stand and the decisive mace duel leave the winners' methods open to dispute even as military resistance collapses.
stories.instruction: Let the final contest resolve control while leaving an ethical claim unresolved, and make characters disagree about what counts as a legitimate win.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Sauptika Parva (Ashwatthama's Night Attack)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Ashwatthama's night attack destroys lives after the main battle appears settled, showing revenge's capacity to outlive formal victory.
stories.analysis: Ashwatthama's night attack destroys lives after the main battle appears settled, showing revenge's capacity to outlive formal victory.
stories.instruction: After an apparent ending, let an unresolved actor exploit a specifically reduced defense, making the new harm follow from earlier choices.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Stri Parva (Lament of Queens & Gandhari's Curse)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.place: Kurukshetra — the field of the dead
stories.teaser: The lamenting women and Gandhari's response shift attention from battlefield achievement to the families and futures it destroys.
stories.analysis: The lamenting women and Gandhari's response shift attention from battlefield achievement to the families and futures it destroys.
stories.instruction: Revisit the outcome through people excluded from the winning decision, giving each a concrete loss and a claim on the survivors.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Shanti Parva (Bhishma's Discourse on Dharma and Governance)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: Bhishma's teachings address the difficulty of ruling after destruction, turning succession into a burden of judgment rather than a final reward.
stories.analysis: Bhishma's teachings address the difficulty of ruling after destruction, turning succession into a burden of judgment rather than a final reward.
stories.instruction: Make a new ruler face competing duties in reconstruction, and use advice through concrete cases rather than uninterrupted exposition.

stories.title: Mahabharata: Mahaprasthanika Parva (Ascent of the Pandavas to the Himalayas)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Mahabharata traditionally attributed to Vyasa; layered textual tradition
stories.teaser: The Pandavas' last journey strips away companions and worldly position, testing how attachment and judgment operate near death.
stories.analysis: The Pandavas' last journey strips away companions and worldly position, testing how attachment and judgment operate near death.
stories.instruction: Use a final journey to revisit earlier values through successive losses, and give the surviving character a last choice that tests loyalty.

stories.title: Bhagavata Purana: Rasa Lila (The Divine Dance of Krishna)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The Rasa Lila presents Krishna's relation to the gopis within devotional theology; union and absence carry meanings beyond ordinary courtship.
stories.analysis: The Rasa Lila presents Krishna's relation to the gopis within devotional theology; union and absence carry meanings beyond ordinary courtship.
stories.instruction: If adapting its formal pattern, distinguish theological symbolism from secular romance and use alternating presence and absence to structure longing.
notes: A devotional theological narrative; formal techniques are not a claim to exhaust its religious meaning.

stories.title: Devi Mahatmyam ( दुर्गासप्तशती - Slaying of Mahishasura & Sumbha-Nisumbha)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Devi Mahatmyam, embedded in the Markandeya Purana
stories.teaser: The Devi's battles present divine feminine power confronting threats that other powers cannot overcome; the episodes differ in adversaries and tactics.
stories.analysis: The Devi's battles present divine feminine power confronting threats that other powers cannot overcome; the episodes differ in adversaries and tactics.
stories.instruction: Give a shared crisis a form of resistance the existing order lacks, and vary each confrontation's strategy rather than only its scale.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Madhu and Kaitabha
children.analysis: The opening episode situates the Devi's power in the conditions that enable Vishnu's response to cosmic danger.
children.instruction: Make an apparent rescuer depend on an enabling power usually overlooked, giving that source of support narrative importance.

children.title: Mahishasura
children.analysis: Divine powers manifest in the Devi to confront an adversary the existing arrangement has not overcome.
children.instruction: Define why established actors fail, then make the new response differ in kind rather than merely increase the same force.

children.title: Shumbha and Nishumbha
children.analysis: The later battles join multiple divine manifestations to the Devi's assertion of power against possessive adversaries.
children.instruction: Use multiple forms as distinct tactical expressions of one underlying capacity, keeping their relationship clear through repeated motifs.

stories.title: Gita Govinda (Jayadeva)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Jayadeva's poem develops Radha and Krishna's estrangement and reunion through songs, mediation, and devotional-erotic imagery.
stories.analysis: Jayadeva's poem develops Radha and Krishna's estrangement and reunion through songs, mediation, and devotional-erotic imagery.
stories.instruction: Organize scenes around changing emotional positions and a mediator's choices, making reunion depend on a recognizable shift rather than repeated yearning.

stories.title: The Turtle Who Couldn't Stop Talking (Kacchapa Jataka)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The turtle's transport works only while he keeps his mouth closed; reacting to taunts breaks the mechanism supporting him.
stories.analysis: The turtle's transport works only while he keeps his mouth closed; reacting to taunts breaks the mechanism supporting him.
stories.instruction: Make a character's habitual reaction directly incompatible with the rescue method, and establish the operating condition before temptation appears.

stories.title: Kapota-Jātaka (The Pigeon and the Greedy Crow)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The crow's appetite drives deception and entry into a kitchen, while the pigeon's restraint supplies a contrasting response to temptation.
stories.analysis: The crow's appetite drives deception and entry into a kitchen, while the pigeon's restraint supplies a contrasting response to temptation.
stories.instruction: Give two companions access to the same temptation, and make the greedy choice require a lie that increases exposure to consequences.

stories.title: Takka-Jātaka (The Ascetic and the Woman)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The Takka tale depicts an ascetic's entanglement with a woman and subsequent betrayal within a historically misogynistic cautionary frame.
stories.analysis: The Takka tale depicts an ascetic's entanglement with a woman and subsequent betrayal within a historically misogynistic cautionary frame.
stories.instruction: Extract a specific conflict between commitment and dependence, but ground deceit in an individual's motives rather than generalizing about gender.
notes: Historically gendered cautionary framing must not be generalized into claims about women.

stories.title: Kuṇāla-Jātaka (Dispute Over Irrigation Water)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The irrigation quarrel occurs in the framing material associated with Kunala Jataka; the full work contains many other stories and themes.
stories.analysis: The irrigation quarrel occurs in the framing material associated with Kunala Jataka; the full work contains many other stories and themes.
stories.instruction: Start with a divisible resource, show how identity and insult increase the dispute's stakes, and give mediation a concrete way to compare costs.
notes: The irrigation conflict belongs to framing material; the entire Kunala Jataka is not synonymous with that episode.

stories.title: Godha-Jātaka (The False Ascetic and the Lizard - Jataka 325/326)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: In Godha Jataka 325, an ascetic's appetite turns a respectful relationship with a lizard into attempted predation; 326 is a different tale.
stories.analysis: In Godha Jataka 325, an ascetic's appetite turns a respectful relationship with a lizard into attempted predation; 326 is a different tale.
stories.instruction: Give a trusted role observable standards, then let changed behavior reveal a concealed appetite before the target commits to danger.
notes: Supplied numbering 325/326 is corrected: Godha is 325; Kakkaru is 326. Other Godha tales also exist.

stories.title: Mahakapi Jataka (The Monkey King's Sacrifice)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The monkey king uses his body to enable the troop's escape, making leadership a concrete assumption of others' risk.
stories.analysis: The monkey king uses his body to enable the troop's escape, making leadership a concrete assumption of others' risk.
stories.instruction: Give a leader a rescue plan that benefits dependents at personal cost, and distinguish voluntary sacrifice from demanding it of others.

stories.title: Vessantara Jataka (The Great Charity of Prince Vessantara)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: Vessantara's radical giving extends into family relationships, making generosity and obligations to dependents difficult to separate.
stories.analysis: Vessantara's radical giving extends into family relationships, making generosity and obligations to dependents difficult to separate.
stories.instruction: Test a celebrated virtue against another person's welfare, and give affected dependents a perspective rather than treating them only as proof of virtue.

stories.title: Banyan Deer Jataka (Self-Sacrifice for the Herd)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Buddhist Jataka traditions; title and numbering require text-specific attribution
stories.teaser: The deer king offers himself in place of another, bringing a ruler's hunting arrangement into contact with an individual act of compassion.
stories.analysis: The deer king offers himself in place of another, bringing a ruler's hunting arrangement into contact with an individual act of compassion.
stories.instruction: Make an unjust routine visible through one threatened beneficiary, then let a voluntary substitution force its administrator to reconsider the whole system.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Burning House (Chapter 3)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Children absorbed in play must be drawn out of a burning house; promised vehicles make urgent instruction intelligible to them.
stories.analysis: Children absorbed in play must be drawn out of a burning house; promised vehicles make urgent instruction intelligible to them.
stories.instruction: Give a guide an audience whose immediate priorities differ from the danger, and make the chosen appeal legible within that audience's existing desires.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Poor Son (Chapter 4)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: An estranged son is gradually prepared to recognize an inheritance he initially cannot imagine accepting.
stories.analysis: An estranged son is gradually prepared to recognize an inheritance he initially cannot imagine accepting.
stories.instruction: Let a character's capacity to receive responsibility grow through bounded tasks, making eventual recognition the result of preparation rather than a sudden announcement.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Medicinal Herbs (Chapter 5)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: Rain nourishes different plants according to their capacities, using ecological comparison to explain differentiated reception of teaching.
stories.analysis: Rain nourishes different plants according to their capacities, using ecological comparison to explain differentiated reception of teaching.
stories.instruction: Give several characters the same opportunity and show differing outcomes through established needs and capacities, avoiding a single universal response.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Conjured City (Chapter 7)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: A conjured city provides exhausted travelers a temporary resting point on a longer journey; the refuge is useful without being the destination.
stories.analysis: A conjured city provides exhausted travelers a temporary resting point on a longer journey; the refuge is useful without being the destination.
stories.instruction: Create an intermediate success that restores capacity, then disclose its limits without making the earlier effort meaningless.

stories.title: The Lotus Sutra: Parable of the Pearl in the Garment (Chapter 8)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: A person lives in deprivation without knowing a jewel is already sewn into their garment, making recognition rather than acquisition decisive.
stories.analysis: A person lives in deprivation without knowing a jewel is already sewn into their garment, making recognition rather than acquisition decisive.
stories.instruction: Plant an overlooked resource in the protagonist's established history, and make discovery change practical choices instead of merely producing instant wealth.

stories.title: Buddhacarita (Acts of the Buddha) (Aśvaghoṣa)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.teaser: The prince's encounter with suffering changes what royal security can mean, leading to renunciation and a search for liberation.
stories.analysis: The prince's encounter with suffering changes what royal security can mean, leading to renunciation and a search for liberation.
stories.instruction: Let encounters expose a problem the protagonist's privileged environment cannot solve, and make departure pursue a new definition of success.
notes: Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: The prince encounters suffering
children.analysis: Encounters with age, sickness, and death challenge the adequacy of a carefully protected royal life.
children.instruction: Let repeated encounters expose different limits of the protagonist's existing worldview, changing what they believe success must address.

children.title: The great departure
children.analysis: Leaving palace life makes the search for liberation a choice involving real attachments and duties.
children.instruction: Give departure identifiable beneficiaries and people left behind, and show why remaining cannot answer the central problem.

children.title: Ascetic practice and awakening
children.analysis: The path tests severe practices before a different understanding of liberation, making persistence distinct from repeating an ineffective method.
children.instruction: Let committed effort reveal a method's limit, and make changing approach arise from evidence rather than convenient inspiration.

stories.title: The Epic of Gilgamesh (Tablets I–XII)
stories.section: Asian & Eastern Sacred Epics, Scriptures & Narrative Poems
stories.attribution: Ancient Near Eastern literary tradition; text-specific versions
stories.teaser: Enkidu's death redirects Gilgamesh from heroic achievement toward mortality; the failed search for lasting life reshapes attention to human limits.
stories.analysis: Enkidu's death redirects Gilgamesh from heroic achievement toward mortality; the failed search for lasting life reshapes attention to human limits.
stories.instruction: Make the loss of a partner invalidate the protagonist's former success metric, then let the quest test possible substitutes before a revised commitment.
notes: Tablet XII is treated as an appended/parallel textual layer; child records are narrative units, not a claim to reproduce all twelve tablet boundaries.
Expanded into selected independently useful narrative units; not an exhaustive chapter-by-chapter or regional-variant catalogue.

children.title: Gilgamesh's rule and Enkidu's creation
children.analysis: The city's suffering under Gilgamesh precedes Enkidu's creation as a counterforce.
children.instruction: Make a powerful protagonist's unchecked conduct generate an opponent whose strengths expose the protagonist's limits.

stories.analysis: Erec's response to accusations of inactivity takes Enide through dangerous tests, exposing tensions between public reputation and mutual trust.
